verdict.reasoning: Transcript: patient reports diarrhoea for three days but never specifies that it is watery. Quote: "I mean … like diarrhoea … it's lasting for like three days." No stool consistency is described.

Transcript: "I need to go like every… I… when I finish, I need to, I feel I need to go again" and later "I… going to the toilet every, ten minute." This supports very frequent episodes with urges recurring soon after bowel movements.

Location and relief are supported, but tenderness and mild severity are not stated. Transcript: "the pain is mainly … in the centre area of the abdomen, like under the belly button" and "it seems to be alleviate a bit, toilet"; there is no description of tender on palpation or that it is mild.

Transcript indicates the vomiting was not immediately after eating fruit: "I had some fruit… And afterwards, I didn't have anything, then I got a bit of nausea, and I vomited". Also, the patient is unsure if there was only one episode. No clear statement limits it to a single emesis.

Transcript: decreased intake – "I try not to eat a lot because… going to the toilet every, ten minute"; possible mild dehydration – "maybe I'm not drinking enough water… I think I don't drink enough water"; unsure about fever – "I'm not sure if I had bit of fever… but I don't think so, I don't know maybe."

No chest pain: "no, I haven't, I haven't noticed any chest pain". Walking/talking OK: patient says both walking and talking are OK though limited by toilet needs. Baseline asthma symptoms: "I always have problems with my breathing, because of the asthma… apart of the normal, I haven't" [no extra problems].
Transcript: "I have, I have, I have a, asthma" clearly documents a history of asthma.
Transcript: "I take some… inhaler" and later "my inhaler kind of run out… I bought a new one here" confirms inhaler use, brand unspecified, and a recent switch to a new one.
Transcript: "I have an allergy. I have N, N, NK, NKDA allergy" is a somewhat confused phrasing but clearly references NKDA, which means no known drug allergies.
Transcript: "my father… he died about um, ten years ago of bowel cancer" confirms paternal bowel cancer and death 10 years ago.

The doctor suspects gastroenteritis: "you might have eaten something bad… this is normally called gastroenteritis". However, the fact adds "watery" diarrhoea, which is not documented, and labels pain as mild and emesis count as single, which are not specified.

Transcript supports risk of dehydration: patient has ongoing diarrhoea, vomiting, and reduced intake ("I think I don't drink enough water"; "I try not to eat a lot"). Doctor advises: "drink lots of water and fluids, because you're losing lots at the moment," indicating concern for dehydration.

Asthma stability: "I always have problems with my breathing, because of the asthma… apart of the normal, I haven't" indicates no worsening. Continued inhaler use is implied: he uses an inhaler and has obtained a new one; no interruption is mentioned.

Anxiety: patient states, "this is kind of uh, my, my worries" about his father's bowel cancer. Doctor: "less likely to be something your father had" and focuses on infection, with no red-flag features like blood in stool, severe pain, or marked systemic illness described.

Transcript: "Number one is to drink lots of water and fluids, because you're losing lots at the moment." While oral rehydration solutions and "small, frequent sips" are not explicitly mentioned, increasing oral fluids is clearly advised.
Doctor advises rest at home: "please stay home for the time being until you get slightly better." There is no mention of a BRAT diet or specific bland diet guidance, so that component is added.
Transcript: "Normally, things like antibiotics don't help, they make the situation worse" directly supports not using antibiotics.

Doctor mentions fever and worsening as reasons to seek help: "make sure and look out for any fevers" and "if you feel you're getting much worse, then I would suggest you go and see your GP". There is no detailed list including blood in stool/vomit, persistent vomiting, escalating pain, explicit dehydration signs, or a 3–4 day duration threshold.
While ongoing inhaler use is implied from history, there is no explicit plan instruction such as "continue using inhaler as needed" in the management discussion.

Follow-up for worsening/no improvement is partially supported but not the specific timing or CRC screening. Transcript: patient says he will "wait a couple of days… or one more day, and then I will book"; doctor agrees but does not specify 1–2 days or mention colorectal cancer screening or discussing screening with GP.
